Both commits are in place, and nothing was merged. The working tree was clean when I started, and I'm back on the starting branch, `feat/2.1.327-next`.

- **`side` branch:** it has a commit that changes line 1 of `plans/rebuild/README.md` to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (side)`.
- **`feat/2.1.327-next`:** it has a commit that changes the same line to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (main line)`.

**Is `side` an ancestor of `feat/2.1.327-next`?** No. `git merge-base --is-ancestor side HEAD` reported that it is not. Each branch has its own commit on top of the shared starting point, so they have diverged.

**Would merging `side` into it conflict?** Yes. `git merge-tree --write-tree` is a dry run that doesn't touch the working tree or index. It reported a content conflict in `plans/rebuild/README.md` (exit code 1), because both branches changed the same first line differently.

The graph output also lists a few other branch tips (`702f2148a` and `579054ee7`, with commit subjects that look like earlier retitle commits). I didn't create or touch those.
